title: CloudWatch Alarm State Changes

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:cloudwatch:events` events with `detail-type="CloudWatch Alarm State Change" detail.state.value="ALARM"` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.1.31 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:cloudwatch:events` traffic without `detail-type="CloudWatch Alarm State Change" detail.state.value="ALARM"`. Confirm UC-4.1.31 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudwatch:events` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.

detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:cloudwatch:events`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `detail-type` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Create EventBridge rule for CloudWatch Alarm State Change. Send to SNS topic; ingest via Splunk_TA_aws or HEC. Filter for state=ALARM. Correlate alarm name with resource tags for ownership.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch:events" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch:events" detail-type="CloudWatch Alarm State Change" detail.state.value="ALARM"
| table _time detail-type source detail.eventName
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.31_cloudwatch_alarm_state_c_31"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudwatch:events` in `index=aws` to detect cloudwatch alarm state changes. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `detail-type` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_31_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Table (alarm, state, reason), Timeline (alarms over time), Single value (active alarms)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of cloudwatch alarm state changes so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
